'''''Daucus edulis''''' ([[Portuguese Language|Portuguese]]: '''''Cenoura-da-rocha''''') is a critically endangered species of flowering plant in the [[celery]] family [[Apiaceae]]. It is [[endemic]] to [[Madeira]].<ref name="CoL" />

==Description==
''Daucus edulis'' is a long-lived perennial plant, up to {{convert|1|m|ft}} in height. It has a hard woody unbranched stem with annual flowers and light yellowish-green, markedly shiny radial leaves, broadly triangular at the edges with pubescent petioles. It has scattered, paniculate [[inflorescences]]. Its fruits are {{convert|10|-|14|x|5|-|7|mm|in}}, oblong to ellipsoid, pubescent and pale when ripe.<ref name=uma>{{cite web |title=Monizia edulis Lowe |url=http://www3.uma.pt/biopolis/planta.php?id=254 |website=www3.uma.pt |access-date=28 November 2020}}</ref>

The species was previously known as ''Monizia edulis''.<ref name="CoL" />

==Distribution and habitat==
The species is endemic to [[Madeira Island]] and [[Deserta Grande Island]] and was once native to the [[Savage Islands]].<ref name="CoL" /> In 2008 its population was estimated to be around 50 individuals in a {{convert|226|sqkm|sqmi}} area.<ref>Jardim et al. in: Martín et al. 2008</ref> It extends from the Central Mountain Massif of Madeira and occupies rocky cliffs and terraces with soil accumulations up to {{convert|300|m|ft}} [[Height above sea level|a.s.l.]] in Deserta Grande<ref>Jardim et al. in: Martín et al. 2008</ref> and up to {{convert|1500|m|ft}} in Madeira.<ref name=iucn /><ref name=uma />

It is mainly threatened by the introduction of exotic species, human collection, fires, droughts, storms, and landslides.<ref>Jardim et al. in: Martín et al. 2008</ref><ref name=iucn />
